changes: weekday normalized: 'roja 3' = day 3 of the week, counted from Sunday, so Tuesday (maṅgalavāra)
notes expanded: the era is just 'samvat' and VS is inferred; possible readings of the corrupt name ending are listed

notes: The colophon writes only 'samvat'. VS is inferred from the size of the year (1891) and the miti/vadi/roja formula, which belongs to Gorkha-period Nepal and North India. If the year were NS it would fall in 2771 CE, which is impossible. Kārttika vadi 4 VS 1891 falls around October/November 1834. 'roja 3' counts weekdays from Sunday, so it means Tuesday. The ending of the scribe's name, '-vatās(!)', is corrupt. It may be a garbled vernacular agent marker (e.g. something like '-vatā' or '-dvārā') or a scribal slip. The stem Dhairyanārāyaṇa is secure and matches the catalogue field. No owner, commissioner or place is named.
